interpreted_intent: Requester meaning: independently select a distinct random concept suited to the linked school-life topic, use the attached portrait, then test a generated image. The actual prior requesting-user topic quote is 학원물; I interpret this through general knowledge as school-life fiction centered on students and their shared school environment. My arm allocation, realistic school community and self-government, is coordinator staging scope rather than requester-owned meaning. Authorial choice: an after-class university student-council vote to convert a spare room into a common study lounge. I compared an election ballot count with an open show-of-hands meeting; the latter makes collective agency readable through large body relationships and avoids dependence on tiny ballot markings. The chair is portrayed using visible facial and bob-hair appearance from the reference; no actual identity, age, biography or personality is inferred. All characters, their ages 21 to 24, their institutional roles, clothing, count, room plan, vote and emotional responses are invented staging, replaceable within the required school-life meaning. The intended experience is the modest pleasure of students taking responsibility for a place they share. The chair notices support, the two raised hands create an already-visible answer, and the minute taker makes the shared decision feel consequential. The saved sensual=1 remains a subtle everyday appeal through natural facial light and an easy presence; fetish=0 and surreal=0 add no treatment. Creativity=1 favors a restrained believable scene. Reference use is appearance guidance, with clothing, body and original camera composition independently authored. Raised hands are kept large and separated from the chalkboard, with the chair and voters on comparable depth planes; the exact proposal cannot be proven by the image without its sketch/title and remains optional narrative context.
subject: A fictional 21-year-old university student using the portrait as face-and-hair appearance reference, chairing three fictional fellow students aged 21 to 24; these numbers, roles and ages are authorial.
setting: An author-chosen university classroom after lessons, its desks temporarily arranged for a student meeting.
event: Everyday school life in progress; the specific chosen realization is a student-council show-of-hands vote while one classmate records minutes.
visual_priorities: The reference-informed chair turns toward the voters, her three-quarter face and short bob individually legible.
Two raised hands and the chair’s directed response form one clear collective decision across the table.
Classroom desks, lesson books and a large student-council heading establish a school community using its teaching room for self-government.
The minute taker and open notebook support the sense that the response is becoming a shared decision without competing with the chair and raised hands.
baseline_prompt_en: A school-life photograph observes students sharing a school day, a small scene of everyday campus life in a university classroom after lessons. The central student is a 21-year-old woman using the supplied portrait as facial and short-hair appearance reference: retain the individual facial proportions, dark eyes, short dark bob and fine separated fringe visible in that reference. She presides over a student-council vote about converting an unused room into a shared study lounge. Four classroom desks form a square meeting table; the students occupy three sides, leaving the camera-side edge open. The central student sits on the right, two classmates aged 21 to 24 sit along the far edge, and a fourth student of the same age range keeps the minutes on the left. The two voters each raise one hand above shoulder level. Their raised hands are separate against the plain chalkboard. The chair turns toward them with attentive eyes and the beginning of a pleased smile, one forearm resting on the tabletop and her other hand open toward the voters. Her face is seen in three-quarter view; her short bob moves slightly as she turns. The minute taker writes in an open notebook. A large chalkboard heading reads STUDENT COUNCIL above a simple floor-plan sketch; stacked lesson books and the classroom window frames establish the ordinary teaching room around this temporary meeting. The central student wears a softly textured navy cardigan over an ivory shirt, with natural skin detail and an easy, unforced presence. Photograph from the open side at seated eye height in a medium-wide horizontal composition: her face and the two raised hands carry the frame, while the notebook and chalkboard remain readable supporting context. Keep the group on a shallow arc at a comparable distance from the lens. Late-afternoon window light crosses their faces softly, with neutral shadows, warm wooden desks and a lived-in documentary texture.
